questions.q: A friend placed the Gita at the bottom of a pile of scriptures to test Swami Vivekananda. What does the article draw from his reply, “The foundation is really good”?
options: A person who refuses to be provoked can turn a negative situation into a positive one
Yes. The author calls this a forgotten teaching of Islam as well.
Humour is the best reply to an insult
Not quite. The article says: A person who refuses to be provoked can turn a negative situation into a positive one.
Sacred books should never be stacked
Not quite. The article says: A person who refuses to be provoked can turn a negative situation into a positive one.
Hinduism is older than other religions
Not quite. The article says: A person who refuses to be provoked can turn a negative situation into a positive one.
questions.rationale: “If an individual simply refuses to be provoked, he becomes so strong that he can turn any negative situation into a positive one.”

questions.q: What is the author’s own view of the differences between religions?
options: They are an evil that dialogue must remove
Not quite. The article says: They are a blessing, if accepted with a positive mind so that people learn from one another.
They make debate the only meeting point
Not quite. The article says: They are a blessing, if accepted with a positive mind so that people learn from one another.
They are an illusion; all religions say the same
Not quite. The article says: They are a blessing, if accepted with a positive mind so that people learn from one another.
They are a blessing, if accepted with a positive mind so that people learn from one another
Well done. He asks for partnership, not rivalry.
questions.rationale: “Differences in religion are not an evil but a blessing. We require only an acceptance of these differences with a positive mind, so that we can learn from each other and live as partners, rather than as rivals.”

questions.q: When the angels questioned the creation of Adam, God explained His plan instead of showing displeasure. What rule of conduct does the article take from this?
options: Never question those in authority
Not quite. The article says: Meet an objection by clarifying the facts, not with anger or personal attack.
Leave disagreements for time to settle
Not quite. The article says: Meet an objection by clarifying the facts, not with anger or personal attack.
Meet an objection by clarifying the facts, not with anger or personal attack
Exactly. And once the truth is clear, accept it at once.
Answer objections with silence
Not quite. The article says: Meet an objection by clarifying the facts, not with anger or personal attack.
questions.rationale: “If anyone objects or disagrees with any issue then it should not be responded to negatively or with personal attacks; instead, the issue must be clarified.”

questions.q: A man asked the Prophet for one piece of “master advice” to manage all the affairs of his life. What was the answer?
options: Give away your wealth
Not quite. The article says: Do not be angry.
Do not be angry
Right. It means responding positively even when provoked.
Pray through the night
Not quite. The article says: Do not be angry.
Speak only when asked
Not quite. The article says: Do not be angry.
questions.rationale: “The Prophet replied, ‘Do not be angry.’ It means that we must not react with anger even when provoked.”

questions.q: What should a wise person do with bitter memories, according to the article?
options: Keep them as a reminder to be careful of people
Not quite. The article says: Deliberately forget them, as a traveller pulls out a thorn and walks on.
Share them with trusted friends
Not quite. The article says: Deliberately forget them, as a traveller pulls out a thorn and walks on.
Deliberately forget them, as a traveller pulls out a thorn and walks on
Yes. Retelling grievances builds a negative personality.
Record them so they are not repeated
Not quite. The article says: Deliberately forget them, as a traveller pulls out a thorn and walks on.
questions.rationale: “A wise person is one who deliberately forgets the bitter memories of the past, and who does not let his mind become a jungle of bitter thoughts.”

questions.q: Why, according to the article, do many intelligent people stay away from religious work?
options: They have no time left after their studies
Not quite. The article says: They are drawn to immediate gain, and find it hard to set aside the ego.
They are drawn to immediate gain, and find it hard to set aside the ego
Correct. The article separates this kind of intelligence from wisdom.
Religious people do not welcome them
Not quite. The article says: They are drawn to immediate gain, and find it hard to set aside the ego.
They find religious teachings too difficult
Not quite. The article says: They are drawn to immediate gain, and find it hard to set aside the ego.
questions.rationale: “It is the attraction of immediate gain… Another trait associated with this kind of intelligence is egoism, which has no place in religion.”

questions.q: What is the article’s position on reading science into the Quran?
options: Scientific study weakens faith in the Quran
Not quite. The article says: The Quran is a book of guidance, not science, though science can deepen our understanding of some verses.
Science and the Quran deal with unrelated things
Not quite. The article says: The Quran is a book of guidance, not science, though science can deepen our understanding of some verses.
Every verse holds a hidden scientific fact
Not quite. The article says: The Quran is a book of guidance, not science, though science can deepen our understanding of some verses.
The Quran is a book of guidance, not science, though science can deepen our understanding of some verses
Well reasoned. We must separate reality from exaggeration.
questions.rationale: “The Quran is not at all a book of science… However, it is true that modern scientific research facilitates our understanding of the Quran.”

questions.q: On what basis will salvation be given, according to the verses quoted in the article?
options: Descent from a prophet’s family
Not quite. The article says: Each individual’s own deeds, not membership of any group.
Belonging to the last revealed religion
Not quite. The article says: Each individual’s own deeds, not membership of any group.
The prayers of others on one’s behalf
Not quite. The article says: Each individual’s own deeds, not membership of any group.
Each individual’s own deeds, not membership of any group
Yes. The Quran lists Muslims alongside other communities without special status.
questions.rationale: “Salvation will not be awarded generally to any group, but on the basis of personal merit… man shall have only that for which he strives.”

questions.q: What does dhikr – the remembrance of God – really mean, in the article’s explanation?
options: To recite the Quran in a fine voice
Not quite. The article says: To think about God so that His presence fills heart and mind.
To pray only in a mosque
Not quite. The article says: To think about God so that His presence fills heart and mind.
To repeat His name a fixed number of times
Not quite. The article says: To think about God so that His presence fills heart and mind.
To think about God so that His presence fills heart and mind
Right. It is spontaneous, “as singing does to a bird.”
questions.rationale: “In the Quran, dhikr, does not mean merely the repetition of words. It means to think about God often.”

questions.q: The Treaty of Hudaybiya looked like a one-sided defeat. Why does the commentary say the Quran called it “a clear victory”?
options: Ten years of peace opened the way for the free exchange of ideas, where monotheism prevailed
Exactly. The contest moved from the battlefield to the field of thought.
The Muslims were allowed to enter Makkah at once
Not quite. The article says: Ten years of peace opened the way for the free exchange of ideas, where monotheism prevailed.
The Quraysh paid compensation
Not quite. The article says: Ten years of peace opened the way for the free exchange of ideas, where monotheism prevailed.
The Muslim army grew stronger for the next battle
Not quite. The article says: Ten years of peace opened the way for the free exchange of ideas, where monotheism prevailed.
questions.rationale: “The end of fighting was in fact synonymous to the opening of the door of dawah… rivalry shifted to the field of intellect.”
